method: Unchanged frozen fixtures, native pinned MiniLM, 384 dimensions, threshold .3, limit eight, 1000-token packets and two-word scale 11/12. Select on development and crate contracts before exposed reserved scoring. Baseline retrieval and final candidate rebuilt with the same constant-age evaluator; all outputs replayed afresh.
limitations: All 26 development gains involve the same OnnxMiniLm component in correlated composed cases. No independent semantic, precision, multilingual or live-agent claim.
Unrequested trailing context can change under existing focused coverage. Per-fact fixture retention is not a universal relevance guarantee.
Concurrent checks are not a latency benchmark.

clock_control.diagnosis: The archived fixed November 7 claim timestamp aged across a UTC-day boundary. An unchanged baseline rerun reproduces the changed overflow negative IDs, so stored baseline reuse is time-dependent.
clock_control.policy: Use the same evaluator for baseline and candidate, setting all fixture claim times to 36 hours before the case starts. This fixes whole-day recency at one with twelve hours of margin, without changing production scoring, inputs, IDs, cutoffs or labels.
clock_control.comparison: Rebuild baseline with unchanged retrieval and the shared clock fix, then replay all baseline and candidate views afresh. Do not use the earlier uncontrolled-clock candidate outputs for acceptance.

discarded_outputs: All preliminary uncontrolled-clock candidate outputs, including the prematurely started reserved subset, were excluded. The development mismatch reproduced on unchanged baseline code; no scope or cutoff was selected from reserved results. Both runtimes and all final comparisons use the shared constant-age evaluator.
